summary.intent: Identify M4 research items that could be pulled into M3, then plan and research Phase 35 (migrating the staging TEE from a local Docker simulator to real Phala testnet infrastructure).
summary.outcome: Phase 35 was scoped, added to the M3 roadmap on a new feature branch, researched in depth, and a RESEARCH.md + VALIDATION.md were written and committed. AWS Nitro TEE (M4 Phase 27) was identified as a future M3 candidate, deferred until after Phase 35 establishes a real Phala baseline.

repo: M4 phases form a tight dependency chain (Billing → Teams → Editors → Signing) and none can be extracted independently into M3.
AWS Nitro TEE was deferred from M2 and again in M4; it depends only on Phase 12 (already shipped) and is a strong M3 candidate after Phase 35.
Staging TEE is currently a simulator/mock running on the same Docker host as the API — not real Phala infrastructure.
TEE worker has minimal test coverage: only 1 test file for 13 source files, with only SSRF validation tested (CONCERNS.md:216-221).
Switching from simulator to CVM produces entirely different keys for the same epoch; staging migration requires wiping ipns_republish_schedule and re-enrolling.
Phala Cloud provides a `phala deploy` CLI that auto-detects existing CVMs by name and can be integrated into the existing deploy-staging.yml GitHub Actions workflow.

code.finding: Uses `keyResult.asUint8Array().slice(0, 32)` — but dstack SDK v0.5.7 may have changed the return type of getKey() from `{ asUint8Array(): Uint8Array }` to `{ key: Uint8Array }`, requiring verification and defensive handling.
Mounts `/var/run/tappd.sock` (dstack OS 0.3.x legacy). Current dstack OS 0.5.x uses `/var/run/dstack.sock` — must be updated for Phala CVM deployment.
Already has a `TEE_MODE=cvm` code path that dynamically imports `@phala/dstack-sdk` and calls `DstackClient.getKey()` — minimal code changes needed for CVM mode.

workflow: GSD plan-phase workflow: when no CONTEXT.md exists and scope is already well-defined from prior discussion, research can proceed without a discuss-phase step.
Phase directories must be manually created before plan-phase can initialize — the workflow doesn't auto-create them.
Research agent returns findings as a task notification with output file path; planner should read the output file before committing.

friction: The plan-phase workflow attempted to read plan-phase.md multiple times (8 reads) before successfully initializing — likely a pagination or offset issue reading a large workflow file.
Phase directory didn't exist and had to be created manually before the workflow could proceed.
The assistant initially started reading CONCERNS.md and environment docs while the researcher was still running, creating parallel work that risked duplication.
open_items: AWS Nitro TEE (M4 Phase 27) still needs to be formally moved to M3 — deferred until Phase 35 establishes a working Phala testnet baseline.
dstack SDK v0.5.7 `getKey()` return type needs runtime verification before tee-keys.ts is updated.
Phala Cloud free tier adequacy for a lightweight Express server needs confirmation.
Key persistence across `phala deploy` re-deployments (same CVM name preserving app_id) must be verified.
TEE test coverage gap: IPNS signing, key management, epoch rotation, and auth middleware are all untested — flagged as High priority in CONCERNS.md.
Production migration path for epoch key transition (simulator → CVM) needs future design; staging can wipe + re-enroll but production cannot.
Phase 35 PLAN.md files have not yet been created — transcript ends after VALIDATION.md commit, before the planner agent was spawned.
